original_card.question: Can a template or call contract leave two or more unpaid coordinates per live family?
methods: State a replacement for the coverage identity (mass = 72W + 64N) and the contract change that realizes it, with its implementation cost.
Find an obstruction: show which data-endpoint obligation forces exactly one unpaid coordinate in the current template.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An explicit replacement identity, verified on a small complete instance with dirty inputs, priced with ceiling.ceiling(unpaid=...). A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

original_card.first_experiment: Explain where the single unpaid coordinate per family comes from in the hosted template; propose one change and price it. Ideal budget: two unpaid coordinates per family is 3.77x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: The deficit is one coordinate per family minus the centre charge; doubling unpaid coordinates per family scales it directly.
allowed_variations: One template change or one endpoint-contract change.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Counting a coordinate as unpaid while leaving it unadvanced in the data endpoint.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: For the exact 34-channel PR3335 P112 scalar fitting factorization, does any change of basis on one triple of channels, with a 3x3 matrix over {-1,0,1} invertible over Q, reduce the inherited full-plane one-total copy invoice below 224?
scope_change_reason: The current paired-plane status closes the orthogonal-local class at invoice 224, above its 160-unit ideal allowance. The only algebraic escape under the same tariff must mix supports across nonorthogonal planes so terms can cancel. I test the smallest nontrivial latent-channel gauge block while preserving the exact scalar fitting matrix, before any larger search or physical implementation.
bottleneck_link: A reduction below 160 would be the first exact rank-34 factorization in this family to pass the favorable zero-overhead plane-port copy screen; a negative result closes every signed-ternary gauge acting on at most three channels of this published factorization. Neither outcome supplies the dirty-state physical decoder or selected supplier.

boundary.source: The 112 selected P112 scalar ports and the exact 34-channel PR3335 factorization K=A A^T, with source columns and reader rows indexed by those ports.
boundary.operation: Choose three of 34 latent channels and an invertible signed-ternary matrix S. Replace their source columns by A S and reader rows by S^-1 A^T; leave the other 31 channels fixed.
boundary.preserved: The complete rational 112x112 fitting matrix K, hence its scalar endpoint and all dirty scalar input columns.
boundary.priced: For each transformed rank-one term, the exact F2 pairing rank between the complete source-plane span and complete reader-plane span; count every term occurrence.
boundary.not_supplied: A physical native word, borrowed-helper restoration, chronological owners, consumer, precision, all-size compiler, or complete supplier interface.

proved: The basis change preserves K exactly whenever S is nonsingular over Q.
The complete-plane one-total pairing tariff is reconstructed from the selected label archive and rematched plane certificate.
All 3^9 signed-ternary matrices and all channel triples are classified by their source and inverse-reader support maps.
unknown: Whether an arbitrary rational or larger-block gauge can reduce the invoice.
Whether any priced scalar factorization has an affordable physical dirty-state implementation and consumer.
obligation_ledger.not_zero_cost_claim: No physical or supplier cost is assigned zero; this is an algebraic tariff screen only.

stop_rule: Stop after enumerating all 19,683 signed-ternary 3x3 matrices, classifying every rationally invertible matrix by exact source/inverse support, and pricing each distinct support map on all 5,984 channel triples. Require an exact 112x112 rational preservation fixture and a wrong-inverse negative control. Do not expand to four-channel searches or native implementation in this package.
evidence: There are 11,808 rationally invertible signed-ternary 3x3 matrices and 396 distinct source/inverse support maps. Across 5,984 channel triples this gives 2,369,664 exact tariff cases. The local invoice delta is never negative: minimum total remains 224, with 520,608 cases tied at 224 and all others costing 225 through 238. The dense rational control checks all 12,544 entries and rejects using S in place of S^-1.

checks: Full signed-ternary census under normal and optimized Python.
Two focused unit tests: 3x3 map census, exact rational matrix identity, singular and wrong-inverse controls.
